content: Twent runs on Android 8.0+ and gives you a real AI assistant that can see your screen, control any app, run shell commands, browse the web, manage files, and connect to external tools — all from one app. The agent can also install MCP servers and skills for itself, delegate to subagents, and ask you for clarification before hard decisions. Download the APK, install Twent, grant permissions, and connect an AI provider — step by step. Extend the agent with MCP servers and Skills. Web research, persistent memory, Agent CLIs, Token Config, and the built-in Ubuntu terminal. Plain-English explanations of every technical term used in these docs. Why Twent exists Most AI assistants live in a chat bubble and can't touch your device. Twent is different — it runs on your phone with full access to the OS, giving AI real agency: reading your screen, tapping buttons, running commands, and managing files. All data stays on your device. BYOK model — your keys, your data. Twent is completely free. Paid model API usage is billed by your chosen provider. If someone asks you to pay for Twent itself, it's a scam. MCP servers, plugins, skills, and workflows for infinite capability. The agent remembers relevant details across conversations, and its memory grows over time. Customize both the app UI and the AI agent's behavior to match your workflow. Zero hidden telemetry. Nothing leaves your device except your explicit API calls. Quick start Follow [Start Using Twent](/getting-started/start-using-twent) — download link, "install unknown apps", and Play Protect workarounds included. Allow everything on the Permissions page, then add an API key under Settings → Model Settings (Nous Research, Opencode Zen, or NVIDIA NIMS are good starts). Open the Terminal page once — setup takes 8–10 minutes and runs by itself. Start the ddg-search server under Plugins → MCP, then ask Twent anything.
description: Twent is a free AI agent for Android — it automates apps, runs an Ubuntu terminal, connects to MCP servers and skills. BYOK.

content: An Agent CLI is an AI agent that runs as a program in a terminal instead of in a chat app — tools like Claude Code or Codex that read, write, and run code for you. The Agent CLIs page of Twent lets you browse all the supported agent CLIs and install them with one tap into the built-in Ubuntu terminal: claude-code codex hermes-agent amp-code pi-agent kilocode …and many more (aider, opencode, gemini-cli, qwen-code, goose, cline, and others) :::tip Make sure your Terminal setup has completed first. :::

title: Agent CLIs

content: Bots are essentially AI agents that are given a specific task — and they keep doing it without you having to ask each time. You can create a bot yourself, or your Twent agent can create one on your behalf. Triggers Each bot runs on one of four trigger types: Manual — no automatic firing; you (or the chat agent) trigger it whenever you want Scheduled — fires automatically on a cron schedule you set Webhook — fires when Twent's local HTTP server receives a matching POST request MCP event — fires when a subscribed MCP server emits a matching event Any bot can also be fired manually at any time — via the calendar page button or by asking the chat agent. Bots can be created by you directly in the bot form, or by the chat agent itself. Managing bots All of your bots appear in the app alongside the agent's work — see the "Bots & Tasks" page for the bird's-eye overview (covered in Subagents). :::tip A bot is just an agent plus a task plus a trigger — describe what should happen and when, and let Twent handle the rest. :::
description: Twent agents with a specific task, triggered manually, on a schedule, by webhook, or by MCP events.
title: Bots

content: The Twent agent can delegate subagents — helper agents that carry out the specific tasks the main agent assigns them. This lets bigger jobs get split into pieces and done while the main agent stays focused on coordinating. Where to see them Bots and subagents can both be viewed from the "Bots & Tasks" page, which gives you a bird's-eye view of everything through a calendar-like UI. Related Bots — scheduled and event-triggered agents you set up yourself
description: The Twent agent can delegate subagents to do tasks in parallel.
title: Subagents

content: The Terminal page is where an entire Ubuntu Linux environment lives, right inside the Twent app. Both you and your agent can use it to install software, run scripts, manage files, and more. First-time setup The moment you open the Terminal page for the very first time after installing Twent, setup starts automatically. It takes about 8–10 minutes, so leave the app open and let it finish. :::note[What gets installed?] Once setup is complete, tap the "Environment Setup" button in the bottom-right corner of the Terminal page to see exactly what was installed during those 8–10 minutes. ::: Many other features depend on this setup being done — including starting MCP servers (Plugins → MCP) and installing Agent CLIs.
description: A full Ubuntu Linux computer inside Twent, with automatic first-time setup.
title: Terminal

content: An API key ("token") is what connects Twent to an AI model provider. The Token Config page lets you get the key for any provider of your choice from that provider's own website, right inside the Twent app — no juggling between your phone browser, email, and the app. Sign up or log in on the provider's page, generate the key, and Twent picks it up. Prefer to configure manually? You can always paste keys yourself under Settings → Model Settings (see Start Using Twent).

content: Everything you need to go from download to your first working AI agent on your phone. If any word below feels unfamiliar (APK, API key, MCP…), click it — every technical term is linked to a plain-English explanation, and they are all collected on the Glossary page. Step 1 · Download the APK An APK is the installation file for Android apps — like a .exe installer on Windows. Download twent.apk (~80 MB) Or copy this address into your phone's browser: https://assets.twent.xyz/twent.apk Step 2 · Allow "Install unknown apps" Because Twent isn't from the Google Play Store, Android blocks installs by default. This is normal — installing apps outside the store is called sideloading. Tap the downloaded twent.apk file. Your phone will say the install is blocked and offer Settings. In that settings screen, turn ON "Allow from this source" for your browser (this is the install unknown apps permission — official Google explanation here). Go back and tap twent.apk again to install. Step 3 · Install Twent Tap twent.apk once more and press Install. :::note[If you see a "Play Protect" warning] Play Protect is Google's scanner — it often flags apps that aren't from the Play Store, even safe ones. To continue: Open the Play Store Tap your profile picture (top right) Tap Play Protect Tap Pause Play Protect and enter your phone password Tap the twent.apk file again to install ::: The same install-and-setup walkthrough video shown on twent.xyz/apk. Step 4 · Grant permissions When Twent opens for the first time you land on the Permissions page. Allow all of them — they power screen reading, automation, files, and the terminal. You can optionally sign in with Google, but there's no added benefit yet. Step 5 · Connect an AI provider Twent is BYOK — bring your own key. An API key is a password-like string that lets Twent talk to an AI model provider, which does the actual thinking. Go to Settings → tap the Model Settings card Pick a Provider, paste an API key, and choose a Model Good options: Provider Get a key from Why pick it Nous Research portal.nousresearch.com Fast responses, very generous free tier, constant free promos Opencode Zen opencode.ai/zen Faster responses, generous free tier NVIDIA NIMS build.nvidia.com Access to many open-weights models; slower responses Step 6 · Wait for terminal setup Open the Terminal page. A full Ubuntu Linux environment sets itself up automatically the first time — this takes 8–10 minutes, so let it run. Details on the Terminal page. Step 7 · Start the web-search server Once the terminal setup is finished, go to Plugins → MCP tab, find the built-in ddg-search server, and start it. This gives the agent web search. More on the MCP page. Done 🎉 You're set. Try asking Twent something, or explore what it can do on Agent Capabilities.

content: App Name: Twent How to Delete Your Data Twent is a local-first application. We do not store your personal data, chat history, or agentic memory on our own servers. All your data is stored locally on your device. To delete your data, please follow these steps: Option 1 (In-App) Open the Twent app, navigate to Settings, and tap the "Clear All Local Data" button. Option 2 (Android System) Go to your Android device Settings > Apps > Twent > Storage & cache > tap Clear Storage (or Clear Data). What Data is Deleted Executing the steps above will permanently and immediately delete all locally stored data, including: Chat history and conversation logs. Agentic memory and knowledge base entries. Saved workflows, templates, and local configurations. What Data is Kept / Third-Party Data Because Twent operates on a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) model, your prompts and files are sent directly to the third-party AI providers you choose (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic). Twent does not retain this data. Any data processed by these third-party providers is subject to their respective privacy policies and data retention practices.
title: Data Deletion Instructions

content: The Twent docs use some technical words. Here's what each one means — the same terms are clickable wherever they appear in these docs. Term What it means APK The installation file for Android apps — like an installer on a PC. Sideloading Installing an app from outside the official Play Store. Play Protect Google's app scanner. It sometimes warns about apps that aren't from the Play Store, even safe ones. Permission A capability you grant an app — camera, storage, seeing your screen, etc. API "Application Programming Interface" — a way for two programs to talk to each other. API key A secret password-like string that identifies you to an online service. Twent uses one to talk to your AI provider. AI model / LLM The "brain" that powers AI chat — e.g. GPT, Claude, or open models like Llama. Provider A company that serves AI models through its API (e.g. Nous Research, NVIDIA). Open-weights model An AI model anyone can download and run themselves. BYOK "Bring Your Own Key" — the app is free; you supply your own provider API key. Ubuntu / Linux terminal A text interface to a full Linux operating system — here, running inside Twent on your phone. MCP Model Context Protocol — an open standard for giving AI agents extra tools (search, GitHub, databases…). MCP server One tool package speaking MCP. Can be hosted online or run locally on your phone. STDIO An MCP server that runs as a local program on your device rather than on the internet. streamable-http An MCP server hosted on the internet that Twent talks to over the network. Skill A ready-made instruction pack that teaches the agent how to do a specific job well. CLI Command-Line Interface — a program you drive by typing commands instead of tapping buttons. Agent CLI An AI agent (like Claude Code) that runs as a CLI program in a terminal.
description: Plain-English explanations of every technical term used in the Twent docs.
title: Glossary

content: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for plugging extra tools into an AI agent. An MCP server can do anything from web search to GitHub management, and Twent speaks it natively. Server types Twent accepts Twent works with two kinds of MCP servers: streamable-http — servers hosted somewhere on the internet; Twent talks to them over the network STDIO — servers that run as a small program right on your phone (inside the built-in terminal) Authentication: the three flavors 1. Browser-based login — some servers let you sign in through a browser flow, like a normal "Log in with…" button. GitHub's MCP server, for example. 2. Auth token — others need you to paste a credential (an API key or access token) into that server's configuration. The Apify server works this way. 3. No authentication — some remotely-hosted servers need nothing at all, like https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp. And some run entirely locally on your phone, like the built-in ddg-search server. Discovering servers You don't have to hunt for configs yourself: Browse and search publicly-published MCP servers from the official MCP Registry — right inside the MCP section of Twent Your Twent agent can also install and run MCP servers on demand, if it thinks one would help with the task at hand Managing servers Everything you've installed appears in the "My Servers" section of the MCP tab Servers can be enabled and disabled from the same tab :::tip[Start here] The built-in ddg-search server gives your agent web search. Start it once your terminal setup has finished — see Start Using Twent. :::
description: Connect your Twent agent to external tools with MCP servers — local, remote-hosted, or authenticated.
title: MCP

content: Skills are ready-made instruction packs that teach your agent how to do specific jobs well — writing styles, workflows, tool recipes. Find them under Plugins → Skills tab. Browsing and installing Browse through and search the skill catalog right inside the Skills tab. Once installed, your Twent agent can call those skills whenever they're useful. Tagging a skill with "/" Want the agent to use a particular skill? Type / at the start of your prompt followed by the skill's name, and Twent will make the agent refer to exactly that skill. Example: typing /copywriting Write a launch tweet points the agent straight at the copywriting skill. My section Everything you've installed appears in the "My" section of the Skills tab. :::note Your Twent agent can also install and use skills on demand — when it thinks a skill would help with what you asked. :::
description: Install skills to teach your Twent agent new behaviors, and call them directly with "/".
title: Skills
